question: How do you access a USB disk connected to the router via network?
expected: By default all the network clients can access all folders on your USB disk. Refer to the following table for access instructions. You can also customize your sharing content and set a sharing account by referring to Customize Your Settings. Windows computer Method 1: Go to Computer > Network, then click the Network Server Name (ARCHER _D7 by default) in the Computer section. Note: Here takes Windows 7 as an example. Method 2: 1. Press Start ( )+ R on the keyboard (or select Start > Run) 2. Type the server address \\tplinkmodem.net or ftp://tplinkmodem.net in the dialog box 3. Click OKs Mac 1. Select Go > Connect to Server 2. Type the server address smb://tplinkmodem.net or ftp:// tplinkmodem.net 3. When prompted, select the Guest radio box 4. Click Connect Note: If you have set up a username and a password to deny anonymous access to the USB disks, you should select the Registered User radio box. To learn how to set up an account for the access, refer to To Set up Authentication for Data Security.
generated:
1. Connect your USB storage device to the modem router’s USB port and wait for the USB LED to become solid on.
2. For Windows computers, go to Computer > Network and click the Network Server Name (ARCHER_D7 by default).
3. Alternatively, press Start + R, type \\tplinkmodem.net or ftp://tplinkmodem.net, and click OK.
4. For Mac, select Go > Connect to Server, type smb://tplinkmodem.net or ftp://tplinkmodem.net, select the Guest radio box, and click Connect.
5. For pads, use a third-party app for network files management.

question: Why might bandwidth control not work as expected?
expected: To use the bandwidth control feature, you’d better set static IP Address on each computer to be controlled or configure Address reservation on the modem router in order to manage easily.
generated:
The problem indicates that the bandwidth control feature may not be properly configured or applied.

1. Ensure that static IP addresses are set for each computer or configure address reservation on the modem router to manage bandwidth control effectively.
2. Verify that the correct total upstream and downstream bandwidth values provided by your ISP are entered in the Bandwidth Control settings.
3. Check that controlling rules are correctly added for each computer, specifying the appropriate IP range and bandwidth allocation.
4. Confirm that the Bandwidth Control feature is enabled and the correct line type (DSL) is selected.
